title: Re-grabbing a release with a previously-imported download hash is removed without re-importing
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing open and closed issues

### Current Behavior

If a release has ever been successfully imported for an episode, and that release is grabbed again later (same download/info-hash — e.g. because the episode's file was deleted and the user wants to redownload it), Sonarr:

1. Never adds the download to the Activity/Queue view, even while it is actively downloading.
2. Immediately reports SonarrStage=Imported for the download via TrackedDownloadService, before the download has even finished transferring.
3. Never actually copies/moves the file into the library (episode stays hasFile: false, no downloadFolderImported event is ever recorded).
4. Once the download completes and its client-side seed/share limit is reached, Sonarr removes it from the download client via DownloadEventHub ("Removing download from qBittorrent history"), believing the job already finished.
5. Because removeCompletedDownloads is enabled (a very common config), the download client then deletes the only copy of the data. Net result: the episode permanently loses the file, with no error, no failed-download entry, and no indication anywhere in the UI that anything went wrong — it just silently reverts to "missing."

This makes it effectively impossible to re-acquire an episode after deleting its file, whenever the same release is grabbed again (which is common, the same uploader/release is frequently the only or best available option for a given episode).

### Expected Behavior

Sonarr should determine SonarrStage/import-needed status based on the episode's current hasFile state (and whether a file actually exists for this download), not solely on historical DownloadHistory/History records keyed by download hash. A previously-successful import event for a given hash should not suppress import of a new download of that same hash once the prior file no longer exists. At minimum, if Sonarr intentionally treats this as "no action needed," that decision should be visible somewhere (e.g. a log line, a queue entry with a clear status) rather than being indistinguishable from a working download that silently vanishes.

To be clear up front: I'm not asking for History/DownloadHistory to be mutated or pruned — a maintainer response on #2393 back in 2019 (https://github.com/Sonarr/Sonarr/issues/2393#issuecomment-453705588) explained why those records are kept immutable forever, and that's a reasonable design choice we're not disputing:

> As we've mentioned before (here/in the linked thread) the status is kept forever because it's part of history, items in history are immutable and aren't meant to be changed, unless the series removed then the history for everything related to that series is removed.

A fix wouldn't need to touch History at all. It would mean TrackedDownloadService (and whatever feeds SonarrStage) determines status primarily from the live state of the specific queue item / download-client entry, using history only as a tie-breaker for genuinely ambiguous cases rather than as a blanket "already handled, ignore" signal whenever the hash matches something historical.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Let an episode be grabbed and successfully imported normally (real downloadFolderImported event recorded, History/DownloadHistory now have an entry for that download's info-hash).
2. Delete the resulting episode file from disk. Trigger RescanSeries (or wait for the scheduled scan) so Sonarr correctly updates the episode to hasFile: false.
3. Trigger a search for the same episode (EpisodeSearch) such that the indexer returns — and Sonarr grabs — the same release as step 1 (same info-hash; this happens naturally whenever the identical torrent/NZB is still the best/only match, which is common).
4. Observe: the download proceeds normally in the download client (qBittorrent, in my case), but:
   - It never appears in GET /api/v3/queue.
   - TrackedDownloadService trace logs show SonarrStage=Imported immediately, even while ClientState=Downloading.
   - No downloadFolderImported history event is ever created.
   - The episode remains hasFile: false throughout.
5. Once the client-side seed/share limit is reached, the download is removed (DownloadEventHub: "Removing download from qBittorrent history"). If removeCompletedDownloads is on, the source file is deleted by the download client. The episode is now permanently missing its file.

I reproduced this cleanly and in isolation twice today(see evidence), confirming it is not caused by any race with a second concurrent download, disk/filesystem issue, or user error — it reproduces with a single, isolated re-grab of a known-good release.

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Alpine 3.23.4 (container), host CachyOS Linux (Arch-based)
- Sonarr: 4.0.19.2979
- Docker Install: Yes
- Using Reverse Proxy: No
- Browser: N/A (API/backend behavior, not UI-specific)
- Database: SQLite 3.51.2
```

### What branch are you running?

Main

### Trace Logs?

Key excerpt from a clean, isolated reproduction today (episode absolute #1156, EpisodeId=2103, release [ToonsHub] One Piece EP1156 1080p NF WEB-DL AAC2.0 H.264 (Multi-Subs), info-hash 23ec1ed6bd7a7417564131922cefd344d69814d9). No other download was active for this episode during this window.

2026-07-08 20:13:36.6|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [One Piece : S23E01 (1156)]. 2 active indexers
2026-07-08 20:13:42.8|Debug|ReleaseSearchService|Total of 53 reports were found for [One Piece : S23E01 (1156)] from 2 indexers
2026-07-08 20:13:48.0|Debug|TrackedDownloadService|Tracking 'qBittorrent:[ToonsHub] One Piece EP1156 1080p NF WEB-DL AAC2.0 H.264 (Multi-Subs)': ClientState=Downloading (readonly) SonarrStage=Imported Episode='One Piece - 1156 WEBDL-1080p v1' OutputPath=.

  -- SonarrStage=Imported reported while the torrent is still actively downloading (0 bytes could
     possibly have been imported yet) and OutputPath is empty. GET /api/v3/queue returns
     {"totalRecords": 0} throughout this entire window.

2026-07-08 20:16:00.1|Debug|TrackedDownloadService|Tracking 'qBittorrent:[ToonsHub] One Piece EP1156 1080p NF WEB-DL AAC2.0 H.264 (Multi-Subs)': ClientState=Completed (readonly) SonarrStage=Imported Episode='One Piece - 1156 WEBDL-1080p v1' OutputPath=/downloads-temp/One.Piece.EP1156.Episode.1156.1080p.NF.WEB-DL.JPN.AAC2.0.H.264.MSubs-ToonsHub.mkv.

  -- Download is now genuinely complete (confirmed: file size matches exactly, client is seeding).
     OutputPath still points at the download-client staging path — it was never copied into the
     library. GET /api/v3/episode/2103 still returns hasFile: false, episodeFileId: 0.

2026-07-08 20:21:00.1|Debug|TrackedDownloadService|Tracking 'qBittorrent:[ToonsHub] One Piece EP1156 1080p NF WEB-DL AAC2.0 H.264 (Multi-Subs)': ClientState=Completed SonarrStage=Imported Episode='One Piece - 1156 WEBDL-1080p v1' OutputPath=/downloads-temp/One.Piece.EP1156.Episode.1156.1080p.NF.WEB-DL.JPN.AAC2.0.H.264.MSubs-ToonsHub.mkv.
2026-07-08 20:21:00.2|Trace|EventAggregator|DownloadCanBeRemovedEvent -> DownloadEventHub
2026-07-08 20:21:00.2|Debug|DownloadEventHub|[[ToonsHub] One Piece EP1156 1080p NF WEB-DL AAC2.0 H.264 (Multi-Subs)] Removing download from qBittorrent history
2026-07-08 20:21:00.2|Trace|EventAggregator|DownloadCanBeRemovedEvent <- DownloadEventHub

Final confirmed end state immediately after the above:
- GET /api/v3/episode/2103 -> hasFile: false, episodeFileId: 0
- No file present anywhere under the series library path for this episode
- The download-client staging file (/downloads-temp/One.Piece.EP1156...mkv) is gone (removed by the client's share-limit action)
- GET /api/v3/queue -> {"totalRecords": 0} throughout the entire episode

### Anything else?

Database evidence (SQLite, read directly from sonarr.db while investigating): the DownloadHistory table shows the same download-hash (23EC1ED6BD7A7417564131922CEFD344D69814D9, same episode as above, from an earlier reproduction earlier the same day) grabbed four separate times over a few hours:

Date (UTC)                  | EventType      | Notes
2026-07-08 19:36:17         | 1 (grabbed)    | First grab
2026-07-08 19:43:17.595     | 5 (imported)   | Real import: sourcePath -> destinationPath both populated, file genuinely copied into the library
2026-07-08 19:43:17.603     | 2              | Recorded ~8ms later
2026-07-08 22:38:11         | 1 (grabbed)    | Re-grab after file deleted
2026-07-08 23:08:58         | 1 (grabbed)    | Re-grab after file deleted again
2026-07-08 23:34:03         | 1 (grabbed)    | Re-grab after file deleted again

Only the first grab has a matching import (EventType=5) event. None of the three subsequent grabs of the identical hash have any corresponding import event — they were grabbed, downloaded, and then simply disappeared once their download-client share limits were hit, exactly matching the trace-log reproduction above.

I also captured a clean control case in the same trace session: a different release for the same episode (different info-hash, never grabbed before) was grabbed concurrently and correctly showed SonarrStage=Downloading while in progress, then imported normally — confirming the issue is specific to hash reuse against stale history, not a general tracking failure.

As a workaround, I manually deleted the relevant rows from History (WHERE EpisodeId IN (...)) and DownloadHistory (WHERE DownloadId IN (...)) for the affected episodes and restarted Sonarr, which did resolve tracking for a fresh grab of a different release — but obviously this isn't a workaround an end user should have to reach for, and doesn't prevent recurrence the next time the same release is grabbed again.

[sonarr_repro_trace.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29827029/sonarr_repro_trace.txt)
